Chosen answerability threshold: **0.54** - minimum expected cost when a wrong automatic reply is counted as 2x the cost of an unnecessary escalation, with 0 automatic replies to never-auto classes.

No threshold reaches 90% automation precision on this data (best with at least 5% automation: 79.8%), because identical ticket texts carry different `answerable_from_docs` labels. Raising the threshold mostly removes correct automations rather than wrong ones.

Sensitivity of the choice to the cost ratio:

| wrong reply cost vs escalation | chosen threshold | auto-answered | automation precision |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x | 0.54 | 72.4% | 77.3% |
| 1.5x | 0.54 | 72.4% | 77.3% |
| 2x | 0.54 | 72.4% | 77.3% |
| 3x | 0.74 | 41.6% | 79.8% |
| 4x | 0.95 | 0.0% | 100.0% |

Intent confidence threshold: **0.30** (out-of-fold intent accuracy 100.0%).

Local TF-IDF retrieval relevance threshold: **0.3360**; top-1 article correct for 97.2% of answerable development tickets.

## Label noise ceiling

Identical ticket bodies in the development set carry different `answerable_from_docs`, `urgency` and `expected_route` labels. Grouping exact duplicates, a perfect text-only system could reach at most ~89% routing accuracy and ~73% urgency accuracy on this data. See docs/discovery_evidence.md.
